question: What is the most appropriate technique to diagnose an infection with Legionella pneumophila ?:

options.opa: Detection of antigen (serogroup 1) in a urine sample.
options.opb: Gram stain of a respiratory sample.
options.opc: Cultivation in blood agar and incubation at 42º C in a microaerophilic atmosphere.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Detection of Legionella pneumophila antigen (serogroup 1) in a urine sample -> specific for Legionella pneumophila infection -> high sensitivity and specificity -> 95%
CHAIN: Cultivation in blood agar and incubation at 42º C in a microaerophilic atmosphere -> Legionella pneumophila grows on specialized media -> definitive diagnosis -> 90%
